title: Company rhythm: OKR rebaseline playbook and 90-day cadence proposal
content:
Purpose:
This is a working playbook for a mid-quarter OKR rebaseline plus a proposed 90-day company rhythm. Goal: give leadership and cross-functional stakeholders a repeatable, low-friction process to adjust priorities, surface risks, and prepare a clean all-hands + exec update that preserves alignment and minimizes churn.

Background / context:
- After the Sep incident and the Dedicated rollout delays, several teams have reported that current Q4 OKRs are no longer realistic.
- The company wants to avoid a full-cascade reset; instead, we propose a scoped rebaseline process for engineering, product, and growth-facing OKRs.
- This doc captures a proposed 90-day cadence, the rebaseline checklist, stakeholder roles, comms templates, and acceptance / rollback triggers.

High-level principles (trade-offs):
- Keep changes surgical: adjust targets (numbers) before changing broad strategic bets.
- Preserve cross-team commitments: any OKR that affects SLAs or Dedicated contracts needs exec sign-off.
- Prioritize measurables and deadlines; remove ambiguous or low-signal activities.
- Timebox decision windows to avoid rolling delays.

Proposed 90-day cadence (quarter-neutral, rolling window):
1) Week -2: Leadership pre-read distributed (current OKR status, heatmap of at-risk items).
2) Week -1: Team-level triage workshops (60–90m): owners list mitigation options and impact.
3) Week 0: Rebaseline decisions (leadership sync + product-eng deep dive).
4) Week 1: All-hands (announce changes, rationale, new commitments).
5) Week 2–3: Cross-functional alignment slots (SRE, Support, Sales enablement).
6) Ongoing: Weekly signal review (tokenized metrics + confidence score)

When to trigger a rebaseline:
- >20% delta vs target velocity for a platform-critical objective (sustained 2 weeks).
- A major incident that materially affects customer SLAs or Dedicated commitments.
- Regulatory or contractual constraints that affect scope.

Rebaseline process (step-by-step):
- Inputs required (owners must submit 48 hours before leadership pre-read):
  - Current objective text, owner, success metrics, baseline and current progress percentage
  - Short rationale for proposed change: (scale back / extend / reprioritize / remove)
  - Mitigations tried and why they failed/succeeded
  - Downstream impacts (customers, billing, partner agreements)
- Triage workshop (team-level):
  - 60 minutes max, facilitator, 2 slides: status + proposed change + options considered.
  - Outcome options: keep, scale back (quantified), pause, or retire.
- Leadership decision criteria:
  - Is the objective still strategically aligned?
  - Does change reduce dependency clashes?
  - Does the proposal preserve customer contracts and SLAs?
  - Is the ROI positive vs other top company bets?
- Decision authority matrix:
  - Executive (CEO + COO + Head of Product): OK to retire/scale back cross-company objectives or anything affecting SLAs/dedicated capacity.
  - GTM leader sign-off required for any customer-facing cadence or pricing-impacting change.
  - Head of Eng + SRE: required for platform/latency objectives.

Communications plan (all-hands + exec updates):
- All-hands runbook (Week 1):
  - 2 slides: Why we rebaselined (data heatmap + customer impact), What changed (list of adjusted OKRs), What you should do (team next-steps).
  - Speakers: CEO (big picture), Head of Product (why), Head of Eng (execution impact), Head of CS (customer Qs).
  - Q&A: pre-submitted questions triaged; 20 minutes live.
  - Internal note (post-event): dedicated Slack thread + updated Confluence page.
- Exec update template (to be circulated after decision):
  - Subject: Decision summary — OKR rebaseline (date)
  - 1-line summary of change, 2–3 bullets with rationale, risk mitigations, and immediate asks.
  - Required attachments: heatmap, list of owners and timelines, customer impact matrix.

Metrics and dashboards to publish with decision:
- OKR health heatmap (green/amber/red) with confidence score (0–100) per objective.
- Token-level cost delta for any inference-related OKR changes (monthlyized).
- Latency P50/P95 and Dedicated capacity utilization projections for the next 90 days.
- Customer-facing commitments table (customer, commitment, impact, owner).

Roles & responsibilities (quick):
- OKR owner: submit inputs, attend triage, propose mitigations.
- Team facilitator: produce 2-slide triage doc.
- Director/Head: validate cross-team impacts.
- Exec decision group: approve retire/scale/extend.
- Comms lead (company-ops): draft all-hands slides, update Confluence, send exec email.

Acceptance criteria and rollback triggers:
- Acceptance (for scaled-back objective): a revised target with acceptance from owners and exec; new milestone plan uploaded to linked artifact.
- Rollback triggers (if we relax a performance guardrail): if the chosen mitigation increases cost by >25% projected, re-evaluate within 30 days.
- Emergency rollback: any customer SLA regression observed for 2 consecutive days triggers immediate exec review and potential partial rollback.

Playbook timeline (example, 3-week run):
- T-14: Owners submission deadline.
- T-12: Company-ops compiles heatmap and pre-read.
- T-10: Team triage workshops.
- T-7: Leadership decision meeting (60m).
- T-5: Draft exec update + all-hands slides.
- T-3: Final review and sign-off.
- T0: All-hands and email.

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: Perceived frequent shifting -> morale hit.
  - Mitigation: Limit to 1 rebaseline per rolling 90-day window; only exec-authorized.
- Risk: Customers confused by changing commitments.
  - Mitigation: Customer comms owner for each affected customer + tailored message.
- Risk: Engineering thrash when targets move mid-execution.
  - Mitigation: Freeze scope changes inside sprint boundaries; only adjust targets, not sprint scope unless critical.

Open questions / decisions to make (working list):
- Should we limit rebaseline authority to strategic objectives only (i.e., exclude small team-level KR tuning)?
- Do we want a separate cadence for Dedicated capacity contractual commitments?
- How to encode confidence scores (who owns scoring rubric)?

Templates appendix (quick snippets):
- Exec email snippet: "We completed a targeted rebaseline of X OKRs to reflect operational realities after the September Dedicated rollout. Key changes: [summary]. Please review owners and timelines attached."
- All-hands speaker notes: one-liner per slide + 2 FAQs.

Immediate next steps (owners):
- Ava: finalize heatmap template and post to Confluence (due 2024-10-22).
- Ravi: schedule triage workshops and collect 2-slide submissions (due 2024-10-25).
- Sofia: draft all-hands run-of-show and coordinate speaker rehearsals (due 2024-10-30).
- Markus: wire up temporary dashboard for OKR health signals (P0: token cost delta, latency, Dedicated utilization).

Notes to self / working ideas (informal):
- Consider a short-term "pause" label for OKRs in flux instead of immediate retirement — gives owners runway.
- Could prototype confidence scoring as composite: progress% * (1 - variance) * cadence factor. Will test with three objectives.
- Keep the communication short: leaders want one slide with the decision and one with the impact.

Appendix: example heatmap rows (tabular view represented in text)
- Objective: Improve inference P95 -> Owner: Mark -> Baseline: 320ms -> Current: 410ms -> Status: Amber -> Proposal: scale back goal to 350ms by EoQ; mitigation: prioritize kernel optimizations.
- Objective: Reduce inference cost per 1k tokens -> Owner: Priya -> Baseline: $0.80 -> Current: $0.95 -> Status: Red -> Proposal: pause quantization experiment rollout; run A/B with 10% traffic.

Document status: DRAFT. Use this as the working playbook for the next rebaseline window. Please add comments inline or ping me in #company-ops for high urgency items.

-- Ava
